problem: VLA policies for mobile robots mostly map observations to actions with implicit reasoning, or parse actions out of generated CoT text with hand-designed rules. That leaves the link between reasoning and executable, embodiment-specific control weak, especially when locomotion and manipulation must be coordinated.
motivation: Long-horizon mobile robots need semantic decisions grounded in physical control across different embodiments. Text-parsing of reasoning outputs is brittle and gives no learnable interface between reasoning and action. The paper therefore adds a learnable decoder over reasoning hidden states and uses RL to make reasoning consistent with the actions it induces.
key_idea: Decode task-level actions (Vx, Vy, ω, behavior primitive) from the VLA's observation and reasoning hidden states with a learnable dual-query cross-attention decoder, train the reasoning with multi-granularity CoT SFT followed by offline GRPO with action-based rewards, and hand the actions to robot-specific low-level controllers.
insight: Both the decoder and GRPO matter. In the component ablation on R2R-CE, SR goes 58.0 (neither) → 63.1 (decoder only) → 68.3 (GRPO only) → 69.8 (both), so GRPO gives the larger gain and the two are complementary. Conditioning the decoder on reasoning states beats conditioning on observations alone (69.3 vs 68.8 SR), and using both is best (69.8). Multi-granularity CoT beats every single granularity (68.3 vs 64.0 for No-CoT), and the reward terms (movement, behavior, format) are complementary. Because the policy outputs embodiment-agnostic task-level actions, it transferred to the Unitree G1 humanoid with no G1-specific training data.
method: Multi-granularity CoT data engine: Gemini-2.5-Flash generates <think>/<answer> traces at episode (18K), step (78K) and navigation (38K) level from R2R, RxR and QUARD. Four-stage filtering (format, action validity, safety/relevance, manual check) reduces 168K raw generations to 134K samples.

Multimodal backbone: LLaVA-style, NaVILA-initialized LLaMA3-8B. It takes RGB, depth (DepthAnything V2) and point cloud (PTv3) tokens, with frozen encoders and trained projection layers plus LoRA (r=16).

Reasoning-conditioned action decoder: two learnable queries (locomotion, behavior) cross-attend over the concatenated observation and reasoning hidden states (single layer, 8 heads, d=4096). A regression head outputs (Vx, Vy, ω) and a softmax head outputs the behavior primitive α.

Two-stage SFT: first on CoT-Episode and CoT-Nav for long-horizon reasoning, then on CoT-Step with the decoder trained jointly. The loss is L_CoT + λ_loc·L_loc (L1) + λ_beh·L_beh (CE), with masks for missing targets.

Offline GRPO: N=8 samples per input; the decoder is frozen and produces the action for each sample. Reward = 1.0·cosine movement + 1.0·exact-match behavior + 0.2·format. Group-normalized advantages, clipped ratio, KL β=0.04, 1K steps.

Embodiment-decoupled execution: task-level commands go to fixed Go2 and G1 low-level locomotion and manipulation controllers (reach, grasp, lift, place primitives). Inference is hybrid, with the 8B model on a remote H20 GPU at 205–245 ms latency.

setting.backbone: NaVILA-initialized LLaMA3-8B VLA with LoRA, plus a reasoning-conditioned cross-attention action decoder (fine-tuned SFT + GRPO)
setting.training_data: MobileVLA-CoT (134K Gemini-2.5-Flash-synthesized reasoning samples derived from R2R, RxR, QUARD); SFT 3 epochs on 4×H20, then offline GRPO for 1K steps; no G1 data
setting.observation: egocentric single-view RGB + depth + point cloud (LiDAR on Go2), plus language instruction
setting.action_space: task-level (Vx, Vy, ω) continuous velocities + discrete behavior primitive α, executed by robot-specific low-level controllers
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE R2R-CE/RxR-CE); QUARD simulator; real Unitree Go2 and G1

numbers.extra: Uses depth and point cloud; trained on extra synthesized CoT data

results: On R2R-CE val-unseen it reaches 69.8 SR and 66.9 SPL, versus 68.3/65.2 for MobileVLA-R1 and 65.1/62.3 for CorrectNav. On RxR-CE it reaches 73.1 SR. On QUARD the average success rate is 0.76 (vs 0.70 for MobileVLA-R1 and 0.60 for MoRE). On the real G1 the full-task success is 56.7%, +10.0 over MobileVLA-R1.
limitations: The action space is task-level (velocities plus a finite set of primitives), so it cannot represent fine contact dynamics or dexterous whole-body manipulation; G1 manipulation uses fixed controller routines.
The 8B model runs on a remote GPU (205–245 ms latency), which depends on network connectivity, and GRPO is offline only.
Transfer to G1 is not general embodiment adaptation, and the gains over MobileVLA-R1 are modest, with small real-world evaluation sets.
